analysis.evidence: עֵמֶק takes הַשִׂדִּים as its complement, forming the place name “Valley of Siddim.” The verse describes the bitumen pits there.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ prefixes a masculine singular common noun in the construct state.

draft.change: Add the Hebrew place name שִׂדִּים with its attested geographical sense.
draft.definition: Siddim is the name of the valley where the kings gathered, identified in Genesis 14:3 with the Salt Sea.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:3 names the gathering place עֵמֶק הַשִּׂדִּים and immediately identifies it with the Salt Sea.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 14:10 describes the bitumen pits in עֵמֶק הַשִׂדִּים, the same valley named in Genesis 14:3. The marked word identifies which valley contained the pits.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes the place name שִׂדִּים, which completes the construct phrase עֵמֶק הַשִׂדִּים, “the Valley of Siddim.”
analysis.sense: The name of the valley identified with the Salt Sea.

analysis.evidence: In בֶּאֱרֹת בֶּאֱרֹת חֵמָר, the marked noun is the first of two identical plurals. The repetition conveys the abundance of pits in the Valley of Siddim, and חֵמָר identifies their contents as bitumen.
analysis.morphology: Feminine plural construct of the common noun בְּאֵר. The initial ב is part of the noun.
analysis.sense: A well or pit in the ground, here one containing bitumen.

analysis.evidence: The marked בֶּאֱרֹת is the second of two consecutive occurrences. It forms a construct phrase with חֵמָר, “bitumen pits.” The repetition depicts the Valley of Siddim as full of such pits.
analysis.morphology: Feminine plural construct of the common noun בְּאֵר, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: A well or pit, here one containing bitumen.

analysis.evidence: In בֶּאֱרֹת בֶּאֱרֹת חֵמָר, the repeated בֶּאֱרֹת emphasizes the many pits in the Valley of Siddim. חֵמָר names the substance in those pits, bitumen.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute common noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah flee in battle and then fall there (וַיִּפְּלוּ שָׁמָּה). The destination הֶרָה, “to the hills,” belongs to the later נָּסוּ, whose subject is the survivors.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol in the third person masculine plural.
Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a standalone place-name article for סְדֹם, keyed by its own consonants סדמ. The supplied root סגר does not account for this form.
draft.definition: סְדֹם is the Hebrew name of the city of Sodom.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:19 names Sodom alongside Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim in its description of Canaanite territory.

analysis.evidence: In מֶלֶךְ סְדֹם, “king of Sodom,” סְדֹם names the city ruled by the king. The following וַעֲמֹרָה pairs Sodom with Gomorrah.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
